title: Tactical winsheet: inference vendor scenarios and rebuttals
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, scenario-driven winsheet for reps and SDRs when evaluating or pitching Redwood against general LLM API providers and managed model endpoints. Focus is on short rebuttal scripts, hard numbers to cite, demo hooks, escalation notes, and a few low-friction technical checks to use during discovery.

Keep it short for quick reference on calls. Use the ‘demo hooks’ during product walkthroughs and ‘tactical traps’ to highlight where Redwood’s production-first posture wins.

Quick competitor archetypes (high-level):
- Commodity LLM APIs (plug-and-play endpoints): pricing-focused, simple onboarding, limited operational controls. Strength: ease of start. Weakness: unpredictable tail latency, limited private deployments, opaque unit economics.
- Cloud-managed model endpoints (cloud vendor offerings): integrated infra, large feature set but heavyweight contract/lock-in. Strength: enterprise integrations. Weakness: cost at scale, inflexible routing/quantization choices.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes & open-source stacks: deep control, but heavy ops. Strength: cost control if you invest ops. Weakness: long TTV, lack of unified support/SLAs.

Key value pillars to call out (one-liners to memorize):
- Predictable unit economics: we give per-token cost breakdowns + tooling (Optimize) to reduce spend without guesswork.
- Production SLAs and fallbacks: reserved capacity + automatic model fallbacks to preserve availability.
- Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private: single integration, many deployment choices.
- Observability for decisions: token-level traces and per-prompt quality regressions tied to evaluations.

Tactical traps (productive ways to steer the conversation):
- When they brag about easy onboarding: "Totally — easy to start is table-stakes. What matters after table stakes is predictable latency and cost when your traffic grows by 10x. How are you forecasting tail latencies and token spend today?"
- When they push price-per-1k-tokens: "Price today ≠ price at 10–100M tokens. We give you batching, KV prefix cache guidance, and quantization recommendations tied to your workload. Want a quick model-level estimate for your current monthly tokens?"
- When they claim single-vendor convenience: "Lock-in simplifies short-term ops, but how do you plan for model heterogeneity, fallback regions, and cost shocks? We treat routing and fallbacks as policy primitives so you can avoid outages when a single model or region degrades."
- When they say 'we can host it ourselves': "Absolutely — we support private/on-prem deployments. The question most teams miss is: who owns the upgrade/rollback SRE runbook? We offer a private control plane and optional professional services to shorten ops risk."

Objection handling snippets (soundbite + follow-up ask):
- Objection: "Your pricing looks higher."
  Rebuttal: "Our per-token rate is only part of the story — we measure cost per successful user action. With our batching + cache suggestions and model recommendations we've seen customers cut token costs 30–60% depending on latency tolerance. Can I run a 2-week cost-savings estimate on your trace?"
- Objection: "We can't move sensitive data to a third party."
  Rebuttal: "Understood. We offer a private deployment option with customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration. If you want, we can scope a proof-of-concept inside your VPC in 2–3 weeks with SOC-level audit hooks."
- Objection: "We already have dedicated capacity from another vendor."
  Rebuttal: "Nice — how are they handling model rollouts and gradual canaries? Our rollout primitives let you split traffic by model version, route on latency or cost, and automatically fallback while retaining token accounting per route. Do you track rollback MTTR for model changes today?"

Demo hooks (what to show in 5–12 minutes):
- Latency trace -> show token-level breakdown on a live short prompt vs a long one; highlight tail latency and batching effects.
- Routing policy editor -> create a simple policy that routes by region and cost tier; show immediate effect on a sample request.
- Rollout / canary -> launch a canary for a new model version and trigger a failover; show metrics before/after and the rollback path.
- Cost delta snapshot -> run Optimize quick-scan and show recommended quantization + batching plan for a sample workload, including estimated % savings.

Suggested metrics & numbers to cite (benchmarks to keep in memory):
- Typical production savings with Optimize: 25–50% token cost reduction depends on mix (cite as range).
- Mean tail latency reduction when using continuous batching + prefix cache: up to 40% on inference-heavy traffic patterns (workload dependent).
- Time-to-PoC for private deployment: 2–4 weeks (includes security review and minimal infra prep).
- SLA and uptime expectations for Dedicated customers: configurable uptime targets with SLO-backed credits (details in SLA doc PRD).

Customer discovery checklist (questions to identify win conditions):
- Current monthly token volume and growth rate? (10k, 100k, 1M, 10M+ buckets)
- Are you using streaming responses or structured outputs (function call style)? How sensitive to per-token latency is the UX?
- Do you have any regulatory constraints (SOC2, HIPAA, data residency)?
- How are you currently handling model rollouts and post-deploy quality checks?
- Cost visibility: do you have per-route/token-level billing right now?

Redlines & escalation paths (when to loop in SE or account exec):
- Loop SE if the prospect asks for per-model latency breakdowns or wants a traced PoC with production traffic.
- Loop Solutions/PS for net-new private deployments, HSM integration, or complex VPC peering.
- Loop Legal for customer requests on contractual SLAs, data residency, or custom compliance clauses.

One-minute opening lines (choose vibe):
- Direct: "We help engineering teams ship predictable LLM features—lower cost, fewer surprises, and the same API whether you deploy with us, on reserved capacity, or in your VPC."
- Story: "Teams often start with a public API but get surprised by cost and tail latency at scale. We built Redwood to make inference predictable across every step of growth."

Short email follow-up templates (for trial/poC asks):
- Template A (PoC acceptance): "Thanks again — next step: a 2-week PoC. We'll need a sample traffic trace, a lead contact for infra, and a short security checklist. We’ll produce a cost-run and a rollout plan by week 2."
- Template B (price pushback): "Totally fair — attached is a short worksheet. If you share a recent token trace we’ll run a quick ‘Optimize’ scan and show a concrete savings estimate within 48 hours."

Competitive differentiators to call out (quick bullets):
- Unified API across hosting modes (reduces integration drift).
- Built-in cost tooling with operational recommendations (not just numbers).
- Routing and fallback policies as first-class primitives (improves reliability).
- Enterprise readiness (KMS/HSM, private control plane, audit logs) + PS.

Appendix: short cheat lines for technical questions
- "Batching vs quantization question": both are orthogonal; we recommend batching first for throughput-sensitive endpoints, then model quantization profiles guided by evals for quality-sensitive flows.
- "Why not pure self-host?": self-host gives control but not the operational acceleration—we reduce MTTR and provide Ops-grade rollouts and tracing so your SREs don't have to reinvent the wheel.
- "How do fallbacks avoid hallucination divergence?": fallbacks prioritize model compatibility and versioned prompts plus canary testing; we tie quality regressions to prompt sets and gate rollouts on eval thresholds.

Notes to rep (quick reminders):
- Always tie cost conversation to a customer action (e.g., successful conversion, doc processed). Raw token prices land poorly without outcome mapping.
- Use demo hooks selectively; pick 1–2 that solve the prospect’s most immediate pain.
- If they push for ultra-low cost only, steer to a conversation about ops ownership and long-term TCO.

Open items for follow-up (internal):
- Update SLA language for Dedicated to include clearer MTTR pledges (product ask).
- Create a one-click ‘cost-scan’ upload flow for sales to drop in a token trace and get an automated Optimize report.
- Gathering two new benchmark cases for enterprise private PoCs (retail search and revenue ops).

End of doc.

Quick edit history: initial draft 2024-11-08 by Aisha; revisions 2024-12-12 (demo hooks tuned) and 2025-01-22 (metrics updated).
